description: UML class-diagram shapes, drawn from scratch in standard notation. Each is placed as the presentation shape custom:uml/<name> (an architecture node gets it from its kind - class, interface, provided-interface, required-interface - but a freeform document has no kind vocabulary, so write shape=custom:uml/class explicitly there): class (a box in three stacked compartments: name, attributes, operations), interface (the same box with an <<interface>> stereotype line), lollipop (a provided interface: a ball on a stem) and socket (a required interface: a half-circle on a stem). A class or interface is ONE node; its members live in the node's props as line lists - props.attributes and props.operations are arrays of strings, one member per string - and its name is the node label. A member's leading + - # ~ is the visibility glyph (public, private, protected, package), so a plain-text member such as "+ save(): void" round-trips as typed. props.stereotype (optional string) replaces the stereotype line; an interface defaults to "interface", a class to none. Compartment heights come from the content (name rows, one row per member, an empty compartment keeps one row) using the metrics below, which the web canvas (web/src/model/umlShapes.ts), the MCP SVG renderer (src/Draughtsman.Mcp/Rendering/SvgRenderer.cs) and the layout sidecar (sidecar/src/layout/elk.ts) all read, so they cannot drift; a box taller than its content gives the extra to the operations compartment. Lollipop and socket are small fixed symbols: the symbol fills the top half of the box, its stem starts at the left edge (the port to connect a realisation or dependency line to) and its label sits in the bottom half. Relationship line-ends (inheritance, aggregation, composition, dependency) are edge styles, not shapes.
